title: Ultimate Strength
summary: We study the buckling of plates and stiffened panels, the progressive collapse of hull girders, and ring-stiffened cylindrical shells, including unsymmetrical bending, neutral-axis rotation, welding residual stress and distortion, damage and heel. ISUM, a differentiable implementation of the Idealised Structural Unit Method in JAX, is under verification.
topics: Progressive collapse of hull girders under combined and unsymmetrical loading, intact and damaged
Ultimate strength of stiffened panels including welding residual stress and deformation effects
Buckling and collapse of ring-stiffened cylindrical shells, including pressure hulls
Plate buckling, neutral-axis rotation and heeling effects in hull-girder strength and residual capacity assessment
Ongoing development: Differentiable reimplementation of incremental collapse methods in JAX, enabling automatic sensitivities of ultimate strength with respect to scantlings and material parameters
lineage: This area continues the incremental-iterative tradition of simplified progressive collapse analysis developed by CS Smith and RS Dow (former Newcastle University Professor in Marine Structures), whose methods for the elasto-plastic collapse of plates and stiffened panels were incorporated into UK naval structural design standards and the submarine design manual, and were later adopted by classification societies for merchant ships. Professor Seo held a post in marine structures at Newcastle University from 2014 to 2017.
methods: Nonlinear finite element analysis in Abaqus; Smith-type progressive collapse methods; ISUM implementation in Python and JAX with automatic differentiation.
short: Buckling and progressive collapse of hull girders, stiffened panels and shells.

title: Fatigue and Fracture
summary: This area concerns structures that already contain a flaw and carry cyclic load, and whether they remain fit for service. We assess flaws against fracture and fatigue criteria, study fatigue crack growth in welded joints, and examine the wave scatter data on which fatigue life estimates depend.
short: Fatigue crack growth, and the assessment of structures that contain flaws.
topics: Engineering critical assessment (ECA) and fitness-for-service evaluation of flawed welded structures
Fatigue crack growth in welded joints, and the influence of weld geometry and residual stress
Hull girder fatigue under revised wave scatter diagrams, and the sensitivity of damage ratios to that choice
Defect assessment for alternative marine fuel containment, including low-temperature toughness of cryogenic steels
Crack initiation and growth in welded steel structures, including the heat-affected zone and weld toe geometry
Hydrogen effects on crack growth in structural steels, and the coupling between hydrogen transport and fracture
methods: Fitness-for-service and engineering critical assessment procedures; fatigue crack growth analysis under revised wave scatter data; peridynamic modelling of crack initiation and growth, including coupling to hydrogen transport.
development: Peridynamics is an emerging method within this area. The lab has no publications on it yet; the first manuscripts are under review.

title: Dynamic Response
summary: Following the mandate of ISSC Committee II.2, this area concerns vibration: the dynamic response of marine structures as it bears on safety, serviceability and habitability, and its uncertainty. We work on transient hull girder vibration and whipping under underwater explosion, the shock acceleration transmitted to equipment, and the modal behaviour of floating offshore wind turbines, including their natural frequencies and damping ratios and the effect of azimuth sampling on both.
short: Vibration of ships and offshore structures: whipping, shock and modal behaviour.
topics: Hull girder whipping under underwater explosion loading, and the effect of hull inelasticity on the whipping response
Shock response and the shock acceleration transmitted to equipment and armament mounts, and its sensitivity to the fracture model used
Modal behaviour of floating offshore wind turbines: natural frequencies, damping ratios, and the rotor azimuth sampling and averaging that determine them
Uncertainty in linearised dynamic models, including the aliasing of tower-passage harmonics and the periodicity discarded by azimuth averaging
Nonlinear structural dynamics and transient response under impulsive loading
methods: Explicit nonlinear finite element analysis in Abaqus; OpenFAST linearisation with multiblade coordinate transformation and Floquet analysis; our in-house packages VANE and pyBModes.
development: Propeller–ice interaction and ice milling is a current student topic, within the mandate’s propeller-induced and ice-induced vibration. The lab has no publications on it yet.

title: Limit States During Accidental and Damage Conditions
summary: We study collision, grounding, impact, blast and underwater explosion through simulations of plate tearing, perforation and structural damage. The fracture models used in those simulations are calibrated in the lab from material tests over a range of stress states and temperatures. We also assess the residual strength of damaged structures.
short: Collision, grounding, impact and explosion: ductile fracture, tearing and residual strength.
topics: Ship collision and grounding analysis with fracture-based failure criteria, up to accidental limit state assessment
Plate tearing and perforation, including the aluminium structures used in high-speed craft
Dropped object impact, and slamming loads on bow and bottom structures
Coupled analysis of collision between floating bodies, where hydrodynamic reaction changes the energy available to damage the structure
Damage extent prediction for in-compartment explosions in warships
Air blast response of marine grade aluminium plated structures
Residual capacity of damaged structures, linked to hull-girder ultimate strength assessment
Calibration of ductile fracture models (Hosford-Coulomb, GTN, BWH instability criteria) for shipbuilding and high-tensile steels
User material subroutines (VUMAT) for shell and solid elements, including the mesh-size regularisation that shell fracture prediction depends on
Localised necking as a separate failure mechanism from fracture, and the strain rate and thermal softening effects that govern it
Material testing across stress states and temperatures, down to sub-zero service conditions
methods: Explicit nonlinear finite element analysis in Abaqus; material testing across stress states and temperatures; calibration of Hosford–Coulomb, GTN and BWH criteria; user material subroutines (VUMAT) for shell and solid elements, with the mesh-size regularisation that shell fracture prediction depends on.

title: Offshore Renewable Energy
summary: We work on floating wind, floating solar and offshore substations, mainly on the integrity of moorings and dynamic power cables. CableDyn computes the global dynamics of mooring lines and cables; CableXsec, under development, analyses the cable cross-section and its fatigue. The floating solar studies cover wave response, connectors and float arrangement.
short: Floating wind, floating solar and offshore substations; mooring and power cable integrity.
topics: Cross-section mechanics of layered power cable constructions, linking manufacturer-level cable design to the stiffness properties used in global dynamic analysis
Shape and curvature of lazy-wave dynamic cables, where fatigue damage concentrates at the sag and hog bends and the touchdown zone
Inter-wire slip and hysteresis in helical armour, measured in moment-curvature tests and resolved component by component
Long-term fatigue assessment of moorings and cables under site-specific metocean conditions, connecting design load case simulation to damage accumulation
Wave-structure interaction of offshore floating solar arrays, including uniform and hybrid connector arrangements
Seakeeping of catamaran and barge float configurations for floating solar
Design challenges and standardisation gaps for floating solar systems deployed at sea
Design challenges, structural integrity and standardisation gaps for floating offshore substations
methods: OpenFAST and OrcaFlex for coupled and line dynamics; our in-house packages CableDyn and CableXsec; Bayesian filtering and surrogate modelling in Python.
funding: Development of Demonstration Technology for Key Mooring Components of 3MW-class Floating Offshore Wind Turbines, Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning, 2026-2029
Development of Evaluation Technology for Reliability Enhancement of Dynamic Submarine Cables, Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning, 2026-2029
projectTitles: Development of Demonstration Technology for Key Mooring Components of 3MW-class Floating Offshore Wind Turbines
Development of Evaluation Technology for Reliability Enhancement of Dynamic Submarine Cables

title: Structural Assessment During Operations
summary: We estimate the loads, structural response and fatigue damage of structures in service from a small number of measurements: platform motions, line-end loads and strains. The methods are virtual sensing, system identification and the inverse finite element method, built on mechanical models. Digital twins for operational assessment are under development.
topics: Physics-based virtual sensing of mooring line tension from platform motion, using Kalman filtering and related state estimators built on lumped-mass line dynamics
Inverse finite element method for reconstructing displacement and damage fields from sparse strain measurement
System identification of cable and mooring response, including uncertainty-aware neural models used as estimators rather than as predictors
Structural digital twins for floating wind, from OpenFAST linearisation and modal identification through to state-space export
Load reconstruction and fatigue monitoring for structural assessment during operations
methods: Kalman and particle filtering; inverse finite element method; NARX and neural system identification; our in-house packages VANE and FOWCON.
funding: Physics-Based Virtual Sensing Methodology for Estimating Mooring Line Tension in Floating Offshore Wind Turbines, Inha University New Faculty Research Grant, 2026-2027
Machine Learning-Based Tension Prediction for FOWT Mooring Lines, Inha University New Faculty Research Grant, 2025-2026
short: Estimating loads and fatigue damage in service from a few measurements.
development: VANE is public and FOWCON is in private alpha. The completed 2025–2026 surrogate-model project is the baseline for the current physics-based virtual sensing project.
projectTitles: Machine Learning-Based Tension Prediction for FOWT Mooring Lines
Physics-Based Virtual Sensing Methodology for Estimating Mooring Line Tension in Floating Offshore Wind Turbines
